correctness.rationale: Uniqueness is in the reduced variable x=sqrt(lambda/mu), not the pair (mu,lambda); all positive pairs with the optimum ratio are equivalent. In the new variables, the entire objective is G(rho,z)=Phi(rho z)+phi(rho z) M(z) since 2x^2=(1-rho^2)z^2/2. Its z derivative is phi(rho z)(1-rho)((1+rho)zM(z)-1). The Mills integral gives 1-zM(z)=integral u exp(-zu-u^2/2) du over u>0, strictly decreasing from 1 to 0. Thus the root determines the unique interior global minimum. At the root G_rho=z phi(rho z)(1-rho zM(z)), giving the asserted exact derivative. For the singular endpoint, expand exp(-u^2/2) to first order with remainder bounded by u^4/8, and integrate against u exp(-zu); this gives 1-zM(z)=z^-2-3z^-4+O(z^-6). It follows that z=rho^-1/2(1+O(rho)), and both terms in the centered minimum contribute phi(0)sqrt(rho) at leading order. At rho=1 the reduced expression is identically 1, while the smooth branch selected by the distinct equation zM(z)=1/(1+rho) has a finite limit z*. The one-sided derivative at 1 is z*phi(z*)/2 and 1-rho=2/(kappa+1), yielding the stated O(kappa^-2) error and the optimizer estimate. Independent numerical check using the Taylor series for the Gaussian integral and exponential brackets z* between 0.61200318096248076 and 0.61200318096248077 and reproduces z*phi(z*) to the shown digits. value.rationale: The singular square-root rise from the sharp threshold and coefficient of the 1/kappa deficit at large thresholds quantify how useful the optimized probability bound is, and the optimizer laws tell how the shape ratio must be tuned to reach it. This is a useful quantitative refinement of an existing optimization problem; the elementary change of coordinates by itself would not warrant a pass.
